```{r blind-switch}
UNBLIND <- as.logical(Sys.getenv("UNBLIND_STUDY4", "FALSE"))
# The blind switch, as in Study4_01_Quant.Rmd. While UNBLIND is FALSE this
# file reads the blind long data file, whose labels are already shuffled,
# shuffles the ratings within each question right after they are read
# (section 2.1), and writes every output to a blind_run/ subfolder of the
# folder its real counterpart goes to.
if (is.na(UNBLIND)) stop("UNBLIND_STUDY4 must be TRUE or FALSE.")

# A blind report belongs in blind_run/, and an unblinded report beside this
# file. The knit: line in the header reads the same environment variable and
# sends the report to the right folder when the file is knitted with
# RStudio's Knit button. A call to rmarkdown::render() must pass
# output_dir = "blind_run" in a blind run and leave it out in an unblinded
# run. A run whose report would land in the wrong folder stops here, before
# anything is written. The folder is read from the settings render() is
# running with; a knit that does not go through render() is not checked.
render_output_dir <- function() {
  frame <- Find(function(e) exists("output_dir", envir = e, inherits = FALSE) &&
                  exists("knit_input", envir = e, inherits = FALSE),
                sys.frames())
  if (is.null(frame)) return(NULL)
  d <- get("output_dir", envir = frame)
  normalizePath(if (is.null(d)) "." else d, mustWork = FALSE)
}
report_dir <- render_output_dir()
if (!UNBLIND && !is.null(report_dir) && basename(report_dir) != "blind_run") {
  stop("A blind report must be written to blind_run/. Knit with the Knit ",
       "button, or run rmarkdown::render(\"Study4_03_Integration.Rmd\", ",
       "output_dir = \"blind_run\").")
}
if (UNBLIND && !is.null(report_dir) && basename(report_dir) == "blind_run") {
  stop("An unblinded report must not be written to blind_run/. Set the ",
       "environment variable UNBLIND_STUDY4 to TRUE before knitting, or run ",
       "rmarkdown::render(\"Study4_03_Integration.Rmd\") without output_dir.")
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                      comment = "#>", fig.align = "center")
```

```{r banner, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (!UNBLIND) {
  cat("**Blind run. The Human and AI labels are shuffled across participants,",
      "the source times across each participant's sources, the modification",
      "levels across the second works made from each source, and the ratings",
      "across the responses to each question, so nothing in this report is a",
      "result.** The report shows only that the code runs, that the fits",
      "converge and that the tables have the right shape. Every output goes to",
      "a `blind_run/` folder.\n")
} else {

}
```

# 0. What this file does

`Study4_02_Text.ipynb` measured the 6,318 justifications without seeing the
label, the source time or the rating. This file joins the label and the
rating back onto those measures and runs what the registration
(`Docs/Preregistration/AsPredicted/Study4_AsPredicted.md`, question 8) names
for the text.

1. Two registered checks on the creativity justifications (section 3). The
   first asks how well the words alone predict the rating and the label in
   participants left out of fitting. The second asks whether AI-arm
   participants reuse their own words across their 18 creativity
   justifications more than Human-arm participants do, relative to the
   overlap with other people writing about the same second work. As in
   Study 1, the registration predicts that they do.
2. The secondary refit (section 4): the registered rating model of
   `Study4_01_Quant.Rmd`, fitted again without the Human-arm participants whom
   the machine-made word list flags for writing that a machine made the work.
3. Three exploratory descriptions (section 5): tone and concreteness from
   published word ratings, topics found by a model given no labels, and the
   words that carry the rating prediction.

Every justification was written after its rating, so none of what follows
says what produced a rating. It describes what people wrote once their
number was chosen.

# 1. Setup

## 1.1 Packages

```{r packages}
# dplyr, tidyr, tibble and readr build and write the tables. lme4 and
# lmerTest fit the mixed models of sections 4 and 5, and emmeans gives the
# contrasts of section 4. Matrix stores the word counts sparsely, keeping
# only the cells that are not zero, and glmnet fits the penalised regressions.
# The two registered checks come from the shared helper text_checks.R.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(readr)
  library(lme4)
  library(lmerTest)
  library(emmeans)
  library(Matrix)
  library(glmnet)
})
```

## 1.2 Paths

```{r paths}
# Every path is found from this file's own folder, which is the working
# directory when the file is knitted. STUDY4_DIR names the Study 4 folder
# instead, and STUDY_SHARED_R the folder of the shared R helpers. Printed
# paths are relative to the Study 4 folder.
STUDY_DIR <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("STUDY4_DIR", getwd()), mustWork = TRUE)

source(file.path(SHARED_R, "fit_status.R"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "text_checks.R"))

mode_dir <- function(dir) if (UNBLIND) dir else file.path(dir, "blind_run")
OUT_STUDY  <- mode_dir(STUDY_DIR)

  tokens       = file.path(NLP_DIR, "study4_text_tokens.csv"),

  topics       = file.path(NLP_DIR, "study4_text_topics.csv"),

)
QUANT_MANIFEST <- file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_quant_run_manifest.csv")
TEXT_MANIFEST  <- file.path(TEXT_TABLES, "study4_text_run_manifest.csv")
missing_inputs <- names(INPUTS)[!file.exists(INPUTS)]
if (length(missing_inputs) > 0) {
  stop("Missing input(s): ", paste(missing_inputs, collapse = ", "),
       ". Knit Study4_01_Quant.Rmd in the same mode and run ",
       "Study4_02_Text.ipynb first.")
}

cat("Tables to:    ", relative_path(OUT_TABLES, STUDY_DIR), "\n")

# The registered constants, as in Study4_01_Quant.Rmd.
SEED         <- 20260421L
EQ_BOUND     <- 0.224
ALPHA        <- 0.05
N_FAMILY     <- 15L
MEASURES     <- c("transformativeness", "essence_change", "creativity")
LABEL_LEVELS <- c("Human", "AI")
TIME_LEVELS  <- c("less than 1 hour", "10 hours", "100 hours")
MOD_LEVELS   <- c("None", "Slight", "Dramatic")
KEY          <- c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension")
```

## 1.3 Run record

```{r run-record}
# The run record stores the SHA-256 checksum of every input (a 64-character
# fingerprint of the file's exact bytes), deletes the previous run's manifest
# now and each output's previous copy before the chunk that writes it, and
# writes the manifest last.
run <- start_run_record(INPUTS,
                        file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_integration_run_manifest.csv"),
                        STUDY_DIR)
write_run_inputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_integration_run_inputs.csv"))
cat("Run identifier:", run$run_id, "\n")

# Each input must be the file its producing run recorded. The long data file
# and the confirmatory family table are checked against the manifest of
# Study4_01_Quant.Rmd in the same mode, and the text tables against the
# notebook's manifest. A manifest on disk means its run reached the end.
if (!file.exists(QUANT_MANIFEST) || !file.exists(TEXT_MANIFEST)) {
  stop("A run manifest is missing. Knit Study4_01_Quant.Rmd in the same mode ",
       "and run Study4_02_Text.ipynb to the end first.")
}
quant_manifest <- read_csv(QUANT_MANIFEST, show_col_types = FALSE)
text_manifest  <- read_csv(TEXT_MANIFEST, show_col_types = FALSE)
recorded <- bind_rows(select(quant_manifest, file, sha256),
                      select(text_manifest, file, sha256))
input_check <- tibble(input  = names(INPUTS),
                      file   = relative_path(INPUTS, STUDY_DIR),
                      sha256 = run$inputs$sha256) %>%
  left_join(rename(recorded, recorded_sha256 = sha256), by = "file") %>%
  mutate(matches_its_manifest = sha256 == recorded_sha256)
print(as.data.frame(select(input_check, input, file, matches_its_manifest)))
if (!all(input_check$matches_its_manifest %in% TRUE)) {
  stop("Some input is not the file its producing run recorded.")
}
cat("The notebook measured", unique(text_manifest$input_file), "\n")
```

# 2. The ratings and the text tables

## 2.1 The ratings, and the blind shuffle

```{r ratings}
# One row per response: the participant, the second work, the measure, the
# rating, the label, the source time and the modification level. A blind run
# reads the long data that the blind run of Study4_01_Quant.Rmd wrote, whose
# label_mode says "shuffled" on every row; an unblinded run needs "real".
long <- read_csv(INPUTS[["long_data"]], na = "", progress = FALSE,
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character(),
                                  k_points = col_integer(),
                                  rating = col_integer()))
expected_mode <- if (UNBLIND) "real" else "shuffled"
if (!all(long$label_mode == expected_mode)) {
  stop("The long data says label_mode ", paste(unique(long$label_mode), collapse = ", "),
       ", and this run needs ", expected_mode, ". Knit Study4_01_Quant.Rmd in the ",
       "same mode first.")
}
ratings <- long %>%
  transmute(id, stimulus_id = work_id, source, image_kind, source_time,
            modification, dimension, item, k_points, rating, label)
stopifnot(nrow(ratings) == 6318, n_distinct(ratings$id) == 117,
          !anyDuplicated(ratings[, KEY]), !anyNA(ratings$rating),
          all(ratings$label %in% LABEL_LEVELS),
          all(ratings$source_time %in% TIME_LEVELS),
          all(ratings$modification %in% MOD_LEVELS))

# The rating carries no label to shuffle, so in a blind run it is shuffled
# itself. Within each question and answer scale (the two six-point items
# form their own group), the ratings are dealt again among the responses.
# Each group keeps its ratings and their spread, and every link between a
# rating and its participant, second work, justification, label, source time
# and modification level is cut. Without this step the parts of this file
# that relate the words to the rating alone, the rating-from-words check of
# section 3.1 and the word weights of section 5.3, would be real results.
# Responses are taken in byte order of their identifiers, and the
# random-number state is put back afterwards.
shuffle_rating_within_scale <- function(df, seed) {
  ord <- order(df$dimension, df$k_points, df$id, df$stimulus_id, method = "radix")
  group <- paste(df$dimension, df$k_points)
  had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
  if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  on.exit({
    if (had_seed) assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv())
    else rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  }, add = TRUE)
  set.seed(seed)
  out <- df
  for (g in sort(unique(group), method = "radix")) {
    rows <- ord[group[ord] == g]
    out$rating[rows] <- df$rating[rows][sample.int(length(rows))]
  }
  out
}

if (!UNBLIND) {
  before <- ratings %>% count(dimension, k_points, rating)
  ratings <- shuffle_rating_within_scale(ratings, seed = SEED)
  after <- ratings %>% count(dimension, k_points, rating)
  stopifnot(identical(before, after))
  cat("Blind run: ratings shuffled within each question and answer scale, seed",
      SEED, "\n")
}
ratings <- ratings %>%
  mutate(label        = factor(label, levels = LABEL_LEVELS),
         source_time  = factor(source_time, levels = TIME_LEVELS),
         modification = factor(modification, levels = MOD_LEVELS))
cat("Responses:", nrow(ratings), "| participants:", n_distinct(ratings$id),
    "| analysed ratings (five-point items):", sum(ratings$k_points == 5), "\n")
```

## 2.2 The text tables and their contract

```{r text-tables}
# Every text table must carry its agreed columns and none of the forbidden
# ones: the label, the source time, the condition, the rating or the text.
# The readers in text_checks.R stop if one does.
FORBIDDEN <- c(TEXT_FORBIDDEN_COLS, "label", "source_time")
MEASURE_COLS <- c("id", "stimulus_id", "stimulus_source", "stimulus_type",
                  "stimulus_modification", "dimension", "n_words",
                  "says_detail", "says_time", "says_skill", "says_concept",
                  "says_prompt", "says_machine_made", "machine_made_reading",
                  "prior_exposure", "anchor_echo", "detail_polarity",
                  "time_polarity", "skill_polarity", "concept_polarity")
TRUE_FALSE_FLAGS <- c("says_detail", "says_time", "says_skill", "says_concept",
                      "says_prompt", "says_machine_made", "anchor_echo")
measures <- read_csv(INPUTS[["measures"]], na = character(), progress = FALSE,
                     col_types = cols(.default = col_character(),
                                      n_words = col_integer()))
check_text_table(measures, MEASURE_COLS, "The measures file", forbidden = FORBIDDEN)
for (f in TRUE_FALSE_FLAGS) {
  stopifnot(all(measures[[f]] %in% c("True", "False")))
  measures[[f]] <- measures[[f]] == "True"
}

wordcounts <- read_text_wordcounts(INPUTS[["wordcounts"]])
vocabulary <- read_text_vocabulary(INPUTS[["vocabulary"]])
tokens     <- read_text_tokens(INPUTS[["tokens"]])

affect <- read_csv(INPUTS[["affect"]], progress = FALSE,
                   col_types = cols(id = col_character(), stimulus_id = col_character(),
                                    dimension = col_character(),
                                    n_content_words = col_integer(),
                                    n_vad_matched = col_integer(), valence = col_double(),
                                    arousal = col_double(), dominance = col_double(),
                                    n_conc_matched = col_integer(),
                                    concreteness = col_double()))
check_text_table(affect, c(KEY, "n_content_words", "n_vad_matched", "valence",
                           "arousal", "dominance", "n_conc_matched", "concreteness"),
                 "The affect file", forbidden = FORBIDDEN)
topics <- read_csv(INPUTS[["topics"]], progress = FALSE,
                   col_types = cols(id = col_character(), stimulus_id = col_character(),
                                    dimension = col_character(), topic = col_integer(),
                                    weight = col_double()))
check_text_table(topics, c(KEY, "topic", "weight"), "The topic file",
                 forbidden = FORBIDDEN)
topic_words <- read_csv(INPUTS[["topic_words"]], progress = FALSE,
                        col_types = cols(dimension = col_character(),
                                         topic = col_integer(), rank = col_integer(),
                                         word = col_character(), weight = col_double()))
check_text_table(topic_words, c("dimension", "topic", "rank", "word", "weight"),
                 "The topic word list", forbidden = FORBIDDEN)

# Every table keyed by response names exactly the responses of the ratings.
response_keys <- function(df) sort(unique(paste(df$id, df$stimulus_id, df$dimension)))
rating_keys <- response_keys(ratings)
for (nm in c("measures", "tokens", "affect", "topics")) {
  stopifnot(identical(response_keys(get(nm)), rating_keys))
}
cat("Every table keyed by response names the same", length(rating_keys),
    "responses as the ratings.\n")
```

## 2.3 Joining the measures to the ratings and the label

```{r join}
# The measures were computed without the label, the source time or the
# rating. They are joined back here on the participant, the second work and
# the question, one row to one row. Both sides must name the same source and
# kind, and the measures' modification level must be the second work's own,
# read from its name; the modification column of a blind run is shuffled and
# is not compared.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_join_check.csv"))
joined <- measures %>%
  inner_join(ratings, by = KEY, relationship = "one-to-one")
stopifnot(all(joined$stimulus_source == joined$source),
          all(joined$stimulus_type == joined$image_kind),
          all(joined$stimulus_modification == sub("^.*_", "", joined$stimulus_id)))
join_check <- tibble(
  rows_in_measures = nrow(measures),
  rows_in_ratings  = nrow(ratings),
  rows_joined      = nrow(joined),
  only_in_measures = nrow(anti_join(measures, ratings, by = KEY)),
  only_in_ratings  = nrow(anti_join(ratings, measures, by = KEY)))
print(as.data.frame(join_check))
stopifnot(join_check$rows_joined == 6318, join_check$only_in_measures == 0,
          join_check$only_in_ratings == 0)
write_csv(join_check, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_join_check.csv"))
```

# 3. The two registered checks, on creativity

## 3.1 How closely the words track the rating and the label

```{r recoverability}
# The first check asks how well the words alone predict the rating, and how
# well they predict the label, in participants left out of fitting. The model
# is ridge regression (a regression that shrinks each word's weight toward
# zero), scored on ten folds grouped by participant, so no participant is on
# both the fitting and the scoring side. A response is about one second work,
# so the stimulus is the source and modification pair, named by stimulus_id.
# The rating is scored by the Pearson correlation between predicted and
# observed ratings. The label is scored by the AUC, the probability that a
# randomly chosen AI-arm response gets a higher predicted probability of the
# AI arm than a randomly chosen Human-arm response, one half being chance.
# Each score has a 95 percent interval from resampling participants and a
# reference from 200 permutations, reruns of the whole check on shuffled
# outcomes. Every setting is Study 1's, set as the defaults of
# text_recoverability(), and the reading rule is recoverability_readings().
# The check is descriptive and enters no correction family.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_wordcount_check.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_recoverability.csv"))

wordcount_check <- check_text_wordcounts(ratings, wordcounts, vocabulary,
                                         stim_cols = "stimulus_id", arm_col = "label",
                                         arm_levels = LABEL_LEVELS)
print(as.data.frame(wordcount_check))
write_csv(wordcount_check, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_wordcount_check.csv"))

recover <- text_recoverability(ratings, wordcounts, dims = "creativity",
                               stim_cols = "stimulus_id", arm_col = "label",
                               arm_levels = LABEL_LEVELS)
recover <- recover %>%
  left_join(recoverability_readings(recover) %>%
              select(dimension, target, predictors, reading),
            by = c("dimension", "target", "predictors"))
stopifnot(nrow(recover) == 5)
write_csv(recover, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_recoverability.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(recover %>% select(dimension, target, predictors, estimate,
                                       ci_low, ci_high, null_95th, status, reading) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
```

## 3.2 Within-person word overlap by label

```{r self-overlap}
# The second check predicts that AI-arm participants reuse their own words
# across their 18 creativity justifications more than Human-arm participants
# do, relative to others writing about the same second work. For each
# participant, the own-word overlap is the mean Jaccard overlap (the words two
# texts share divided by the words either uses) among that participant's
# justifications, and the stranger baseline is the mean overlap of each
# justification with other participants' justifications of the same second
# work. Their difference is regressed on the label with the mean number of
# words as a covariate, so the AI coefficient is predicted positive. The
# interval and p-value come from 2,000 resamples of participants within each
# arm, with the stranger baseline rebuilt in each. One measure is registered,
# so the Holm correction, which keeps the chance of any false positive among
# a set of tests at .05, is over one test. The reading is supported, opposite
# direction or inconclusive.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_selfsimilarity_per_person.csv"))
overlap <- text_self_overlap(ratings, tokens, dims = "creativity",
                             stim_cols = "stimulus_id", arm_col = "label",
                             arm_levels = LABEL_LEVELS)
stopifnot(sum(overlap$by_arm$role == "registered comparison") == 1)
write_csv(overlap$by_arm, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.csv"))
write_csv(overlap$per_person, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_selfsimilarity_per_person.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(overlap$by_arm %>%
                      select(dimension, role, quantity, estimate, ci_lo, ci_hi,
                             p_raw, p_holm, reading, status) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
```

# 4. The secondary refit without participants who write that a machine made the work

## 4.1 Who is left out

```{r machine-made}
# The machine-made reading is "asserted" when a justification states,
# plainly or as an impression, that a machine made the work, and it sets
# aside phrases that are negated or sit in a supposition. A Human-arm
# participant with at least one such justification, on any of the three
# measures, wrote that a machine made the work although the vignette said
# Alex used his own tools, and is left out of the refit. The table counts
# them over all 54 justifications and within each measure.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_machine_made_count.csv"))
human <- joined %>% filter(label == "Human")
count_scope <- function(d, scope) {
  tibble(scope = scope,
         n_human_participants     = n_distinct(d$id),
         n_participants_asserting = n_distinct(d$id[d$machine_made_reading == "asserted"]),
         n_human_responses        = nrow(d),
         n_responses_asserted     = sum(d$machine_made_reading == "asserted"))
}
machine_count <- bind_rows(
  count_scope(human, "all justifications"),
  bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) count_scope(filter(human, dimension == m), m))))
print(as.data.frame(machine_count))
write_csv(machine_count, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_machine_made_count.csv"))

flagged_ids <- sort(unique(human$id[human$machine_made_reading == "asserted"]))
stopifnot(length(flagged_ids) == machine_count$n_participants_asserting[1])
```

## 4.2 The refit

```{r refit}
# The registered model of Study4_01_Quant.Rmd, on each measure:
#
#   rating ~ label x source time x modification + (1 | participant) + (1 | source)
#
# with sum-to-zero contrasts (a coding in which a factor's effects add to
# zero across its levels), restricted maximum likelihood (REML, the usual
# estimator of the variances in a mixed model) and the bobyqa optimizer (the
# routine that searches for the best-fitting values), on the five-point
# items. It is fitted twice here on the same ratings: on every participant,
# and without the Human-arm participants of section 4.1. Each fit gives the
# five registered tests (Slight minus None, Dramatic minus Slight, the
# equivalence of Human and AI within plus or minus 0.224, source time, and
# source time by modification), with Holm's correction over the fifteen
# tests of each sample, exactly as in Study4_01_Quant.Rmd. The table
# sets each test's verdict in the refit beside its verdict on every
# participant. The refit is secondary and decides no hypothesis.
#
# In an unblinded run the fit on every participant is the registered fit of
# Study4_01_Quant.Rmd, and its p-values must equal those in that file's
# confirmatory table. In a blind run the ratings were shuffled again in
# section 2.1, so that comparison is not made.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_secondary_refit_machine_made.csv"))

fit_log <- list()
fit_logged <- function(expr, step, d) {
  res <- fit_with_status(expr)
  fit_log[[step]] <<- bind_cols(tibble(step = step, n_obs = nrow(d)), res$status)
  res
}

SUM_CONTRASTS <- list(label = "contr.sum", source_time = "contr.sum",
                      modification = "contr.sum")
FORMULA <- rating ~ label * source_time * modification + (1 | id) + (1 | source)
TEST_NAMES <- c("Slight minus None",
                "Dramatic minus Slight",
                "Human minus AI, equivalence within plus or minus 0.224",
                "source time",
                "source time by modification")

emm_of <- function(res, spec) {
  emmeans::emmeans(res$fit, specs = spec, data = res$data,
                   lmer.df = "satterthwaite", lmerTest.limit = 20000)
}
tost_p <- function(est, se, df, bound) {
  pmax(pt((est + bound) / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
       pt((est - bound) / se, df, lower.tail = TRUE))
}

five_tests <- function(res, m) {
  base <- tibble(measure = m, test_number = 1:5, test = TEST_NAMES,
                 converged = res$status$converged, singular = res$status$singular,
                 note = fit_note(res$status))
  if (isTRUE(res$status$fit_error)) return(base)
  mc <- as_tibble(summary(emmeans::contrast(
    emm_of(res, ~ modification),
    list("Slight minus None" = c(-1, 1, 0), "Dramatic minus Slight" = c(0, -1, 1)),
    adjust = "none"), infer = c(FALSE, TRUE)))
  lc <- as_tibble(summary(emmeans::contrast(
    emm_of(res, ~ label), list("Human minus AI" = c(1, -1)), adjust = "none"),
    infer = c(FALSE, TRUE)))
  a <- as.data.frame(anova(res$fit, type = "III", ddf = "Satterthwaite"))
  f_terms <- c("source_time", "source_time:modification")
  base %>% mutate(
    estimate  = c(mc$estimate, lc$estimate, NA, NA),
    statistic = c(mc$t.ratio, lc$t.ratio, a[f_terms, "F value"]),
    den_df    = c(mc$df, lc$df, a[f_terms, "DenDF"]),
    p_raw     = na_unless_usable(c(mc$p.value,
                                   tost_p(lc$estimate, lc$SE, lc$df, EQ_BOUND),
                                   a[f_terms, "Pr(>F)"]), res$status))
}

family_for_sample <- function(d_all, sample_name) {
  bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
    d <- d_all %>%
      filter(dimension == m, k_points == 5) %>%
      mutate(id = factor(id), source = factor(source))
    res <- fit_logged(lmerTest::lmer(FORMULA, data = d, REML = TRUE,
                                     contrasts = SUM_CONTRASTS,
                                     control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")),
                      paste0("4.2 registered model, ", sample_name, ", ", m), d)
    res$data <- d
    five_tests(res, m) %>%
      mutate(n_obs = nrow(d), n_participants = n_distinct(d$id), .after = measure)
  })) %>%
    mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "holm", n = N_FAMILY),
           holm_significant = p_holm < ALPHA)
}

full    <- family_for_sample(ratings, "every participant")
reduced <- family_for_sample(filter(ratings, !id %in% flagged_ids),
                             "without flagged Human-arm participants")
stopifnot(nrow(full) == N_FAMILY, nrow(reduced) == N_FAMILY)

if (UNBLIND) {
  registered <- read_csv(INPUTS[["quant_family"]], show_col_types = FALSE)
  same <- full %>% select(measure, test_number, p_raw) %>%
    left_join(select(registered, measure, test_number, p_registered = p_raw),
              by = c("measure", "test_number"))
  stopifnot(max(abs(same$p_raw - same$p_registered), na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-8)
  cat("The fit on every participant reproduces the confirmatory table of",
      "Study4_01_Quant.Rmd.\n")
} else {
  cat("Blind run: the ratings were shuffled in section 2.1, so the fit on every",
      "participant is not compared with Study4_01_Quant.Rmd.\n")
}

# A verdict is the Holm decision, and for the two contrasts also the sign of
# the estimate.
verdict_of <- function(tab) {
  ifelse(is.na(tab$holm_significant), NA_character_,
         ifelse(tab$test_number %in% 1:2,
                paste0(ifelse(tab$holm_significant, "significant", "not significant"),
                       ", ", ifelse(tab$estimate > 0, "positive", "not positive")),
                ifelse(tab$holm_significant, "significant", "not significant")))
}
refit <- full %>%
  transmute(measure, test_number, test,
            n_obs_all = n_obs, estimate_all = estimate, p_holm_all = p_holm,
            verdict_all = verdict_of(full)) %>%
  left_join(reduced %>%
              transmute(measure, test_number, n_obs_refit = n_obs,
                        n_participants_refit = n_participants,
                        estimate_refit = estimate, statistic_refit = statistic,
                        den_df_refit = den_df, p_raw_refit = p_raw,
                        p_holm_refit = p_holm, verdict_refit = verdict_of(reduced),
                        converged_refit = converged, singular_refit = singular,
                        note_refit = note),
            by = c("measure", "test_number")) %>%
  mutate(verdict_unchanged = verdict_all == verdict_refit,
         participants_left_out = length(flagged_ids),
         rule = "left out: Human-arm participants with at least one justification whose machine-made reading is asserted",
         family = "fifteen tests per sample, Holm, family-wise alpha .05")
write_csv(refit, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_secondary_refit_machine_made.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(refit %>% select(measure, test, verdict_all, verdict_refit,
                                     verdict_unchanged)))
```

# 5. Exploratory description

Everything in this section is exploratory. It describes what participants
wrote after choosing their rating, and none of it tests a prediction. The
models use the five-point items only, as the registered model does, so that
the rating they hold constant is on one scale.

```{r exploratory-setup}
# The ratings of the five-point items, with the rating centred within each
# question (the rating minus that question's mean rating). Centring makes the
# label coefficient the AI minus Human difference at the average rating.
ratings5 <- ratings %>% filter(k_points == 5)
rating_centres <- ratings5 %>% group_by(dimension) %>%
  summarise(rating_centre = mean(rating), .groups = "drop")
ratings5 <- ratings5 %>% left_join(rating_centres, by = "dimension") %>%
  mutate(rating_c = rating - rating_centre)
CONTROL <- lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
```

## 5.1 Tone and concreteness

```{r affect}
# Each response's mean valence (how pleasant its words are, 1 to 9), arousal
# (how excited they make a reader feel, 1 to 9), dominance (how much in
# control they make a reader feel, 1 to 9) and concreteness (how much they
# refer to things that can be seen or touched, 1 to 5), from Warriner,
# Kuperman and Brysbaert (2013) and Brysbaert, Warriner and Kuperman (2014),
# as the notebook scored them. A response with no matched word has no score
# and drops out of that model. The model is Study 1's, per question and
# measure:
#
#   score ~ label x rating_c + (1 | participant) + (1 | second work)
#
# with the Human arm as the reference. The two label terms of the twelve
# models are corrected together by the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure, which
# holds the expected share of false positives among the rows called positive.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_affect_by_arm.csv"))

AFFECT_MEASURES <- c("valence", "arousal", "dominance", "concreteness")
AFFECT_TERMS <- c("labelAI"          = "AI minus Human at the average rating",
                  "labelAI:rating_c" = "AI minus Human in the slope on the rating")
affect_joined <- ratings5 %>%
  inner_join(affect, by = KEY, relationship = "one-to-one")
stopifnot(nrow(affect_joined) == nrow(ratings5))

affect_by_arm <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  bind_rows(lapply(AFFECT_MEASURES, function(a) {
    d <- affect_joined %>% filter(dimension == m, !is.na(.data[[a]])) %>%
      mutate(score = .data[[a]])
    res <- fit_logged(lmerTest::lmer(score ~ label * rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
                                     data = d, REML = TRUE, control = CONTROL),
                      paste0("5.1 ", a, ", ", m), d)
    base <- tibble(dimension = m, measure = a, term = names(AFFECT_TERMS),
                   quantity = unname(AFFECT_TERMS),
                   mean_Human = mean(d$score[d$label == "Human"]),
                   mean_AI = mean(d$score[d$label == "AI"]),
                   n_scored = nrow(d), n_participants = n_distinct(d$id),
                   converged = res$status$converged,
                   singular = res$status$singular, note = fit_note(res$status))
    if (isTRUE(res$status$fit_error)) return(base)
    co <- as.data.frame(summary(res$fit)$coefficients)[names(AFFECT_TERMS), ]
    base %>% mutate(estimate = co$Estimate, std_error = co$`Std. Error`, df = co$df,
                    t = co$`t value`,
                    p_raw = na_unless_usable(co$`Pr(>|t|)`, res$status))
  }))
}))
affect_by_arm <- affect_by_arm %>%
  mutate(p_bh = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "BH", n = n()), .after = p_raw)
stopifnot(nrow(affect_by_arm) == 24)
write_csv(affect_by_arm, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_affect_by_arm.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(affect_by_arm %>% select(dimension, measure, term, estimate, p_raw,
                                             p_bh, n_scored, converged, singular) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
```

## 5.2 Topics found by a model given no labels

```{r topics}
# The notebook fitted a topic model, a model that finds groups of words that
# tend to occur in the same responses, to each question without the label or
# the rating, and gave each justification a weight on each topic, the
# weights summing to one. The model is Study 1's, per question and topic:
#
#   weight ~ label + rating_c + (1 | participant) + (1 | second work)
#
# Topic weights are bounded between zero and one and pile up at zero, so the
# label term is tested against a permutation null rather than its usual
# standard error. The labels are dealt out afresh among the participants,
# each keeping one label, the model is refitted, and the label term's t value
# is recorded, 200 times in all. The p-value is the share of shuffles,
# counting the observed data as one, whose t value is at least as far from
# zero as the observed one. The same 200 shuffles serve every topic of a
# question, they are drawn from the seed before the parallel section starts,
# and the p-values are corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg within each question.
# Each topic is labelled by its five heaviest words.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_topics_by_arm.csv"))

N_TOPIC_PERM <- 200L
topic_labels <- topic_words %>% filter(rank <= 5) %>% arrange(dimension, topic, rank) %>%
  group_by(dimension, topic) %>%
  summarise(topic_label = paste(word, collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")
topics_joined <- topics %>% filter(!is.na(weight)) %>%
  inner_join(ratings5, by = KEY)

# The label term's t value from one refit; a refit that fails gives NA and
# is counted.
topic_t <- function(d) {
  fit <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
    lme4::lmer(weight ~ label + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
               data = d, REML = TRUE, control = CONTROL))), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NA_real_)
  co <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  if (!"labelAI" %in% rownames(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["labelAI", "t value"])
}

topics_dimension <- function(m) {
  d_dim  <- topics_joined %>% filter(dimension == m)
  id_arm <- distinct(d_dim, id, label)
  id_arm <- id_arm[order(id_arm$id, method = "radix"), ]
  set.seed(SEED)
  shuffles <- replicate(N_TOPIC_PERM,
                        setNames(sample(as.character(id_arm$label)), id_arm$id),
                        simplify = FALSE)
  bind_rows(lapply(sort(unique(d_dim$topic)), function(k) {
    d <- d_dim %>% filter(topic == k)
    res <- fit_logged(lmerTest::lmer(weight ~ label + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
                                     data = d, REML = TRUE, control = CONTROL),
                      paste0("5.2 topic ", k, ", ", m), d)
    usable <- fit_usable(res$status)
    co <- if (isTRUE(res$status$fit_error)) NULL else summary(res$fit)$coefficients
    t_obs <- if (is.null(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["labelAI", "t value"])
    t_null <- text_run_permutations(shuffles, function(lab) {
      dd <- d
      dd$label <- factor(lab[as.character(dd$id)], levels = LABEL_LEVELS)
      topic_t(dd)
    }, text_default_workers())
    n_valid <- sum(!is.na(t_null))
    tibble(dimension = m, topic = k,
           quantity = "AI minus Human in topic weight at the same rating",
           estimate = if (is.null(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["labelAI", "Estimate"]),
           t = if (usable) t_obs else NA_real_,
           p_perm = if (!usable || is.na(t_obs) || n_valid == 0) NA_real_ else
             (1 + sum(abs(t_null) >= abs(t_obs), na.rm = TRUE)) / (1 + n_valid),
           n_perm = N_TOPIC_PERM, n_perm_valid = n_valid, perm_seed = SEED,
           mean_weight_Human = mean(d$weight[d$label == "Human"]),
           mean_weight_AI = mean(d$weight[d$label == "AI"]),
           n_responses = nrow(d), n_participants = n_distinct(d$id),
           converged = res$status$converged, singular = res$status$singular,
           note = fit_note(res$status))
  })) %>%
    mutate(p_bh = p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH", n = n()), .after = p_perm)
}

topics_by_arm <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, topics_dimension)) %>%
  left_join(topic_labels, by = c("dimension", "topic")) %>%
  relocate(topic_label, .after = topic)
stopifnot(nrow(topics_by_arm) == nrow(distinct(topics, dimension, topic)))
write_csv(topics_by_arm, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_topics_by_arm.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(topics_by_arm %>% select(dimension, topic, topic_label, estimate,
                                             p_perm, p_bh, n_perm_valid, converged,
                                             singular) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
```

## 5.3 The words that carry the rating prediction

```{r prediction-weights}
# Section 3.1 asks how well the words predict the rating, with ridge models
# that spread small weights over every word. This asks which words do the
# predicting, with the lasso, a penalised regression whose penalty sets most
# word weights to exactly zero, so only the words a prediction cannot do
# without keep one. As in Study 1, the penalty is chosen by ten-fold
# cross-validation grouped by participant, with the vocabulary floor of five
# responses applied inside each training fold. The chosen penalty is
# lambda.1se, the strongest penalty whose cross-validated squared error is
# within one standard error of the best. The model is then refitted on every
# response at that penalty, and the words with a nonzero weight are reported
# with their signs, one model per question. A positive weight is a word that
# goes with a higher rating. Among words that move together the lasso tends
# to keep one, so a word missing from the list may still go with the rating.
# None of this tests a word.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_prediction_weights.csv"))

prepared <- prepare_text_ratings(ratings5, "stimulus_id", "label", LABEL_LEVELS)
wc_keyed <- wordcounts %>% mutate(.stim = stimulus_key(wordcounts, "stimulus_id"))

lasso_rating_weights <- function(m) {
  fr     <- text_dimension_frame(prepared, wc_keyed, m)
  resp   <- fr$resp
  counts <- fr$counts
  y      <- resp$rating

  set.seed(SEED)
  outer_by_id <- text_participant_folds(fr$id_arm, TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS, LABEL_LEVELS)
  outer_fold  <- unname(outer_by_id[resp$id])

  vocab_all <- text_floor_vocabulary(resp, counts, rep(TRUE, nrow(resp)),
                                     TEXT_WORD_MIN_RESPONSES)
  X_all    <- text_response_word_matrix(resp, counts, vocab_all$word)
  fitted   <- text_with_warnings(glmnet::glmnet(X_all, y, family = "gaussian", alpha = 1))
  full_fit <- fitted$value
  lam      <- full_fit$lambda
  warns    <- fitted$warnings

  fold_loss <- matrix(NA_real_, TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS, length(lam))
  fold_n    <- integer(TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS)
  for (k in seq_len(TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS)) {
    tr <- outer_fold != k
    Xk <- text_response_word_matrix(
      resp, counts, text_floor_vocabulary(resp, counts, tr, TEXT_WORD_MIN_RESPONSES)$word)
    fk <- text_with_warnings(glmnet::glmnet(Xk[tr, , drop = FALSE], y[tr],
                                            family = "gaussian", alpha = 1, lambda = lam))
    warns <- c(warns, fk$warnings)
    pk <- as.matrix(predict(fk$value, Xk[!tr, , drop = FALSE], s = lam))
    fold_loss[k, ] <- colMeans((y[!tr] - pk)^2)
    fold_n[k]      <- sum(!tr)
  }
  cvm  <- apply(fold_loss, 2, weighted.mean, w = fold_n)
  cvsd <- sqrt(apply(sweep(fold_loss, 2, cvm)^2, 2, weighted.mean, w = fold_n) /
                 (TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS - 1))
  i_min      <- which.min(cvm)
  lambda_1se <- max(lam[cvm <= cvm[i_min] + cvsd[i_min]])
  warns      <- unique(warns)

  b <- as.matrix(coef(full_fit, s = lambda_1se))[, 1]
  b <- b[setdiff(names(b), "(Intercept)")]
  b <- b[b != 0]
  words <- if (length(b) == 0) {
    tibble(word = NA_character_, coefficient = NA_real_)
  } else {
    tibble(word = names(b), coefficient = unname(b))
  }
  words %>%
    mutate(dimension = m, target = "rating", .before = 1) %>%
    mutate(sign = ifelse(coefficient > 0, "positive", "negative"),
           rank = as.integer(rank(-abs(coefficient), ties.method = "first"))) %>%
    left_join(vocab_all %>% rename(n_responses_word = n_responses), by = "word") %>%
    arrange(rank) %>%
    mutate(lambda_1se = lambda_1se, lambda_min = lam[i_min],
           n_words_in_model = nrow(vocab_all), n_nonzero = length(b),
           n_folds = TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS, seed = SEED, n_responses = nrow(resp),
           status = if (length(warns) == 0) "ok" else "nonconvergence",
           note = if (length(warns) == 0) "no warning from any fit" else
             paste(warns, collapse = "; "))
}

prediction_weights <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, lasso_rating_weights))
write_csv(prediction_weights, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_prediction_weights.csv"))
for (m in MEASURES) {
  pw <- filter(prediction_weights, dimension == m)
  cat(m, ": ", pw$n_nonzero[1], " of ", pw$n_words_in_model[1],
      " words keep a weight at lambda.1se (status ", pw$status[1], ").\n", sep = "")
}
```

# 6. Fit status

```{r fit-log}
# One row per step that fits a model: the mixed models of sections 4 and 5,
# and the two registered checks, which report their own status (ok,
# nonconvergence or error) from the warnings their fits raised.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_fit_log.csv"))
fit_log_tbl <- bind_rows(
  bind_rows(fit_log) %>% mutate(kind = "linear mixed model",
                                usable = !fit_error & converged),
  recover %>% distinct(dimension, status, note) %>%
    transmute(step = "3.1 recoverability, creativity", n_obs = NA_integer_,
              kind = "ridge regressions", fit_error = status == "error",
              converged = status == "ok", singular = NA, lme4_messages = note,
              usable = status == "ok"),
  overlap$by_arm %>% filter(role == "registered comparison") %>%
    transmute(step = "3.2 within-person overlap, creativity", n_obs = NA_integer_,
              kind = "ordinary least squares", fit_error = status == "error",
              converged = status == "ok", singular = NA,
              lme4_messages = note, usable = status == "ok")
) %>% relocate(step, kind, usable)
write_csv(fit_log_tbl, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study4_text_fit_log.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(fit_log_tbl, step, usable, fit_error, converged, singular)))
lmm <- fit_log_tbl %>% filter(kind == "linear mixed model")
cat("Mixed models:", nrow(lmm), "| converged:", sum(lmm$converged),
    "| singular:", sum(lmm$singular %in% TRUE), "| errored:", sum(lmm$fit_error), "\n")
cat("Registered checks, status: recoverability", unique(recover$status),
    "| overlap", unique(overlap$by_arm$status), "\n")
cat("Prediction weights, status:", paste(unique(prediction_weights$status), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```
